title: Protocol to measure cleavage efficiency of the meiotic cohesin subunit Rec8 by separase in mouse oocytes using a biosensor
protocol: Prepare a 60 mm polystyrene tissue culture dish with 5-6 droplets (around 30 μl each) of pre-warmed medium containing dbcAMP.
Cover the drops completely with a layer of mineral oil.
Prepare another dish/cover/container with a large drop of medium (800-1,000 μL) containing dbcAMP and without oil for dissection of ovaries.
Sacrifice an 8-12 week old female mouse through cervical dislocation or in a CO2 chamber.
Dissect the abdomen and collect the ovaries from the sacrificed mouse.
Carefully tear off fatty tissue with forceps.
Lightly roll the collected ovaries on tissue paper to remove remaining fatty tissue.
Place the ovaries in the dish prepared for dissection (with a large drop of medium containing dbcAMP without oil).
Macerate the ovaries with the sharp tip of a needle, opening up all the large follicles under the binocular microscope equipped with a heated glass plate.
Collect all fully-grown oocytes released from dissected follicles using a glass pipette.
Transfer collected oocytes to a dish with smaller medium droplets (around 30 μL) covered with mineral oil.
Ensure the end of the Pasteur pipette is straight and not too large in diameter for gentle handling of oocytes.
Maintain all steps at 37°C, pre-warming medium and using heated plates on microscopes if necessary.
Denude collected oocytes by passing them through a glass pipette with an inner diameter slightly larger than the oocyte diameter (80–100 μm).
Transfer denuded oocytes to another medium drop in the same dish.
Select fully-grown competent oocytes arrested in prophase I, discarding others that do not meet criteria.
Prepare a microinjection setup including a bright-field microscope with micromanipulators and pipette holders.
Equip the microscope with a heating plate and temperature controller.
Place a depression glass slide on the heating plate.
Connect holding pipette and microinjection needle to pipette holders.
Defrost one mRNA aliquot in an Eppendorf centrifuge at maximum speed for 15–45 min at 4°C.
Centrifuged mRNA is kept on ice after defrosting.
Prepare a microinjection needle.
Load the prepared microinjection needle with 0.5-1.5 μL of mRNA solution.
Microinject mRNA into prophase-arrested oocytes within 15–60 min without additional centrifugation steps.
Make home-made microinjection needles from glass capillaries using a puller.
Load the needle with 0.5–1.5 μl of mRNA solution using microloader tips.
Place a 10-15 μl drop of culture medium containing dbcAMP in the center of a depression glass slide.
Cover the medium drop completely with mineral oil to prevent evaporation.
Transfer oocytes into the medium drop on the glass slide.
Place the glass slide with oocytes under the microinjection microscope.
Lower the holding pipette and loaded microinjection needle to the oocyte level.
Switch the microinjection pump to constant flow setting.
Capture one oocyte with the holding pipette.
Insert the tip of the microinjection needle into the oocyte, avoiding the nucleus.
Quickly take the needle out after injection.
Release the oocyte from the holding pipette.
Repeat steps for microinjecting all oocytes.
Retrieve the needle quickly but carefully while maintaining the same angle to avoid tearing the plasma membrane and killing the oocyte.
Arrange oocytes under the microscope such that non-injected oocytes are above and injected oocytes are below the microinjection needle.
Take one oocyte at a time from the upper pool, move it in front of the microinjection needle for injection, then place it into the lower pool with other injected oocytes.
Transfer the injected oocytes from the glass slide to an unused drop of medium in the original culture dish.
Incubate the transferred oocytes at 37°C for 1–4 hours to allow sufficient time for protein expression.
Adjust incubation duration based on mRNA concentration, length of mRNA sequence to be translated, and efficiency of protein expression.
Prepare a culture dish with 5–6 drops (around 30 μL each) of culture medium without dbcAMP.
Cover the dish with mineral oil and pre-warm it at 37°C.
Place the injected oocytes into several successive drops of culture medium to remove trace amounts of dbcAMP.
Incubate the oocytes at 37°C for 50–70 min until they start undergoing germinal vesicle breakdown (GVBD).
Discard all oocytes still in prophase ten to fifteen minutes after the first oocytes undergo GVBD.
Optional: Prepare a dish with 3–4 drops (around 30 μL each) of medium containing Aurora B/C (or Aurora A) inhibitor (ZM447439 or AZD1152 for Aurora B/C and MLN 8237 for Aurora A).
Cover the dish with mineral oil and pre-warm it at 37°C.
Transfer the required number of injected oocytes that underwent GVBD on time through subsequent pipetting into 2–3 drops of medium with inhibitors.
Leave the oocytes to incubate in the last drop.
Incubate the synchronized batch of oocytes at 37°C for 4–6 h.
Prepare a microscopic chamber as suggested by the microscope manufacturer with multiple drops of 2 μL medium and cover with mineral oil.
Prewarm the microscopic chamber at 37°C.
Place 1–2 injected oocytes in each drop.
If using Aurora kinase inhibitors, use medium containing inhibitors when preparing the chamber.
Place individual oocytes apart from each other to reduce laser exposure during imaging.
Acquire a z-stack of the region around the chromosomes every 15-20 minutes after GVBD at 4–6 h.
Check that the oocytes have survived and control oocytes have extruded a polar body after timelapse imaging.
Using ImageJ, open image sequences for TRANS, 491 nm, and 561 nm channels for one oocyte.
Select oocytes with their chromosomes fully visible during several timepoints before, during, and after anaphase I.
Discard signal from only partially visible chromosomes.
Identify the timepoint of anaphase I marked by chromosome segregation and beginning of polar body extrusion.
Note anaphase onset through attempts of the oocyte to extrude a polar body or sudden movement of chromosomes towards the cortex if Aurora B/C kinases are inhibited.
Consider the timepoint where either event occurs as anaphase.
Measure mean fluorescence on Z-projection at 491 nm and 561 nm channels starting from 3-4 timepoints before anaphase.
Include all chromosomes in the measurement area marked by a box.
Place another measurement box in the cytoplasm away from the chromosomes.
Ensure that the size and position of both measurement areas remain consistent between the two channels.
Follow the movement of chromosomes during anaphase to maintain accurate measurements.
Adjust the measurement area to cover only one half of segregated chromosome masses if necessary, preferably the part remaining in the oocyte.
Import the measurements into MS Excel.
Subtract the “Cytoplasm” from the “Chromosomes” signal for each channel and for each timepoint.
Normalize the result for each channel separately to the timepoint right before anaphase.
Calculate the ratio between the values obtained for the 491 nm and 561 nm channels.
Find the lowest post-anaphase value within 0–30 min after anaphase.
Subtract the lowest post-anaphase value from the highest pre-anaphase value.
This value represents the portion of the sensor that was cleaved during anaphase.
